title: Skill Mismatch in Indian Labour Market and its Impact on Productivity: A Panel Data Analysis
affiliations: University of Burdwan and Narasinha Dutt College

detail.title: Skill Mismatch in Indian Labour Market and its Impact on Productivity: A Panel Data Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no relevant financial or non-financial interests to disclose.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: The authors did not receive support from any organization for the submitted work.

detail.abstract: Skill mismatch of on-the-job workers or he gap between qualification possessed by the worker and the qualifications necessary to perform the work at hand leads to allocative inefficiency and can have serious repercussions for the economy. This mismatch can take two forms – over-qualification (when qualifications possessed is more than required for the job) and under-qualification (when qualifications possessed is less than required). Workers with less skill are less productive while those with excess skill may not work with intended intensity leading to being less productive than optimum as well. In either case, as productive levels suffer, gross output and income levels are also less than optimum, creating impediment on the path of development. In this paper we seek to examine this issue of on-the-job skill mismatch in India with reference to the National Classification of Occupations (NCO) in line with International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO) and National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF). Our first objective is to estimate at the National, State and Sector level, the proportion of workers that are Over-educated/Under-educated for the occupation they are currently engaged in according to the above framework and identify factors that lead to such mismatch between qualification and occupation. In the second part of the study we examine the impact of such mismatch on regional and sectoral productivity differentials using a Panel data framework. The paper adds value on three counts by examining a sparsely researched topic in Indian context. First, we estimate extent of skill mismatch disaggregated by gender, location, social group, skill level, industry, occupation and State – something not done so far. Second, we go further to identify the determinants of mismatch, over-education and under-education separately. Third, we look at the impact of mismatch on Labour Productivity in a Panel data framework, thus incorporating time effect as well. Broad results suggest that more than half of workers in India are under-qualified for the occupation they are in and close to two-thirds suffer from skill mismatch as per the ISCO and NSQF typologies. Mismatch is higher in rural areas, among females and marginal social groups. There is a U-shaped relation between Chances of Mismatch and both Years of Formal Education and Age. The nature of mismatch is however different at the two ends. While at the lower ends, mismatch is mostly because of under-qualification or overemployment, at the higher end mismatch is mostly due to over-qualification or underemployment. Probability of being under-qualified is lowest and that of being overqualified is highest for the casual wage workers indicating that the bargaining mechanism in casual labour market operates as a selective valve barring entry of under-qualified workers but allowing overqualified workers into it – a process that signals presence of a substantial reserve army of overeducated labour in the market. Skill Mismatch, as hypothesised, has a significant negative effect on Labour Productivity. Our counterfactual simulation exercise reveals that allocative inefficiency in the labour market in the form of mismatch between skill possessed by a workers and that demanded by the job in which (s)he is engaged is resulting in 25 per cent loss in labour productivity. The government, industry, and academia should note these issues and reconfigure their programmes to achieve optimum manpower allocation in the economy.

AI.tldr: 印度在职人员技能不匹配问题严重，超过一半工人资质不足，近三分之二存在技能不匹配，导致劳动力生产率损失25%。研究发现技能不匹配在农村地区、女性和边缘社会群体中更为严重，对经济发展造成重大阻碍。
AI.research_question: 印度在职人员的技能不匹配程度如何？导致这种不匹配的因素是什么？技能不匹配对区域和部门生产率差异有何影响？
AI.motivation: 技能不匹配导致配置效率低下，对经济产生严重影响。资质不足的工人生产力较低，而资质过剩的工人可能工作强度不足，两者都会导致产出和收入水平低于最优水平，阻碍发展进程。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于国家职业分类（NCO）、国际标准职业分类（ISCO）和国家技能资格框架（NSQF）的技能匹配理论，分析资质过剩（over-qualification）和资质不足（under-qualification）两种不匹配形式。
AI.method: 使用面板数据框架，首先在国家、州和部门层面估计技能不匹配比例，然后分析不匹配的决定因素，最后考察不匹配对劳动生产率的影响。
AI.findings: 1. 超过一半工人资质不足，近三分之二存在技能不匹配；2. 农村地区、女性和边缘社会群体不匹配程度更高；3. 不匹配与教育年限和年龄呈U型关系；4. 技能不匹配对劳动生产率有显著负面影响，导致25%的生产率损失。
AI.theory_contributions: 1. 首次在印度背景下系统研究技能不匹配问题；2. 按性别、地点、社会群体等多维度分解分析；3. 分别识别资质过剩和资质不足的决定因素；4. 在面板数据框架中纳入时间效应分析生产率影响。
AI.practical_contributions: 为政府、产业界和学术界提供实证依据，建议重新配置人力资源项目以实现经济中最优的人力资源配置，减少25%的生产率损失。

title: Balancing Personalization and Privacy in the New AI Era: The Fate of Data Privacy Protection and Ethical Advertising
affiliations: University of Illinois and University of Illinois

detail.title: Balancing Personalization and Privacy in the New AI Era: The Fate of Data Privacy Protection and Ethical Advertising

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract:
Advertisement is the lifeblood of any business. With technological advancements and the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence, businesses increasingly leverage these tools to reach a broader audience and boost profitability. 

However, a critical concern lies at the heart of this practice: the potential violation of data privacy and associated ethical considerations. This challenge underscores the need to balance personalisation, data protection, and ethical
advertising practices. This paper examines the use and collection of personal data in targeted ads and its implications on privacy rights and the place of ethics in all the issues related to violating privacy rights and unwarranted distribution. It further examines the friction between the protection of data and data privacy vis-à-vis personalised adverts and the need to explore the ethical issues surrounding advertising. 

This study found that in as much as there are legal and institutional regulations on data privacy, the emergence of artificial intelligence has created another gap in the existing laws and modifications of personalised data. In the final analysis,
This paper recommends that collaborative efforts cannot be downplayed between government, business, and consumers to ensure that ethics are maintained in advertising practices, allowing the end users to enjoy using their data without compromising their autonomy.

AI.motivation: 随着人工智能技术在广告领域的广泛应用，数据隐私保护和伦理问题日益突出，需要在个性化营销与隐私保护之间找到平衡。

detail.title: Satisfaction and Continued Partnership Intent of the Restaurant Partners of Zomato: A Latent Variable Computation Model for Sustainable CRM
detail.abstract: Purpose-The food aggregator business in India is a dynamic, fast-growing sector with immense potential for innovation and expansion.This study helps in understanding tier-3 markets in India's digital food industry. This study aims to identify the factors that are responsible for increasing the level of satisfaction vis-à-vis the manifestation of continued partnership intent of restaurant partners and develop a predictive model for various online food aggregators. Thus, it will help the companies to build a better platform to boost restaurant partners' expectations in the long run. Research Design/Methodology-The study is based on primary data collected from 200 restaurant partners who are operating their food business with the help of different platforms namely Zomato and Swiggy in the Durgapur region. Exploratory Factor Analysis and there after Multiple Linear Regression and Binary Logistic Regression in SPSS 20.0 has been used to explore the relationship between the latent constructs and the dependent variable as Satisfaction Rate and Continued Partnership Intent respectively. The study finds a unique and interesting shift of scale with the predicted satisfaction and hence the manifestation of continued partnership intent getting to be dichotomous and therefore the model was further tested for its robustness using the Confusion Matrix and Machine Learning Performance parameters. Findings-The study has identified four basic underlying factors affecting restaurant partner's satisfaction namely concern for On-boarding Dynamics, Order Handling Efforts, Customer Relationship Management(CRM) Efforts, Platform Features. Research limitation/implication-This study was conducted with respondents from the Durgapur region of South Bengal. The study can be extended to other parts of India with more number of respondents and more factors can be unveiled and companies can work upon them effectively.

title: Online Retail: Purchasing Occasional Gifts through Online Channels is a Prevalent Trend in the United Kingdom
affiliations: Wright State University, Wright State University and American International University

detail.title: Online Retail: Purchasing Occasional Gifts through Online Channels is a Prevalent Trend in the United Kingdom
detail.abstract: This study develops and evaluates a predictive model for online gift purchasing behavior in the United Kingdom, utilizing transaction-level data collected from a UK-based online retailer over the period of December 2010 to December 2011. Drawing upon multiple linear regression, the research investigates the extent to which variables such as product type, purchase timing, and unit price influence the quantity of items purchased. The resulting model achieved a highly robust R² value of 0.98599, underscoring its accuracy in capturing consumer behavior within an e-commerce setting. Notably, the model successfully reflects seasonal fluctuations in consumer demand, with particularly pronounced surges during key holiday periods such as Christmas. These temporal spikes emphasize the strong role of cultural and economic factors in shaping online purchasing trends. The findings further reveal distinctive shifts in product popularity across the year, with specific items, such as the White Hanging Heart T-Light Holder, emerging as dominant choices during peak periods. Such patterns demonstrate not only the cyclical nature of gift-oriented consumption but also the importance of symbolic and aesthetic product attributes in influencing purchase decisions. By highlighting both temporal rhythms and product-specific dynamics, the research provides valuable insights into how consumer preferences evolve across different seasonal contexts. In addition to offering empirical evidence of behavioral patterns, this study integrates broader economic and sociocultural perspectives, thereby bridging theoretical frameworks from consumer behavior research with practical retail analytics. The model’s predictive strength enhances its utility for retailers, who may employ these insights to refine inventory management, forecast demand, and design targeted marketing strategies aligned with consumer motivations. Overall, the study contributes to the growing body of literature on predictive modeling in e-commerce by presenting a comprehensive and adaptable framework that underscores the complexity and dynamism of the online gifting market in the UK.

title: Effective Project Leadership Behaviors and their Impact on Project Success
affiliations: University of Johannesburg, Johannesburg, South Africa and University of Johannesburg, Johannesburg, South Africa

detail.title: Effective Project Leadership Behaviors and their Impact on Project Success
detail.abstract: Effective project leadership is widely recognized as a cornerstone of project success, yet there remains limited synthesis of the specific leadership behaviors and competencies that drive performance across industries. This systematic review aimed to identify and evaluate the key leadership behaviors, competencies, and contextual factors that contribute to project success, with particular attention to adaptive, emotional, and relational dimensions of leadership. Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of Google Scholar, Web of Science, and Scopus was conducted for studies published between 2014 and 2023. After removal of duplicates and screening, 93 studies were included for analysis. Data were extracted on study characteristics, leadership behaviors, competencies, emotional intelligence dimensions, adaptive behaviors, contextual challenges, and leadership development interventions. Descriptive and thematic synthesis methods were applied. Of the 7,611 initial records, 93 studies met the inclusion criteria. The temporal analysis showed a surge in publications between 2020-2023, with a peak in 2022 (32.7%). Most studies were indexed in Scopus (55.8%) and Web of Science (42.3%). Industry representation was led by construction (26.9%) and IT (21.2%), with healthcare (11.5%) and engineering (15.4%) comparatively underrepresented. The most frequently reported leadership behaviors were problem-solving (40.4%), decision-making (32.7%), and active listening (26.9%). Collaboration (55.8%) emerged as the dominant leadership competency, while emotional intelligence dimensions-particularly social skills (36.5%) and empathy (34.6%)-were emphasized as critical enablers of leadership effectiveness. Adaptive behaviors such as resilience (38.5%) and flexibility (34.6%) were also frequently highlighted. Contextual challenges included lack of experience (34.6%), high-stress environments (32.7%), and organizational politics (32.7%). Leadership coaching (53.9%) was the most widely reported intervention, followed by executive education (32.7%) and PMP leadership modules (13.5%). This review demonstrates that effective project leadership extends beyond technical expertise, requiring an integration of cognitive, relational, and adaptive competencies. Problem-solving and decision-making remain central to project performance, but collaboration, social skills, and resilience are increasingly recognized as essential to navigating dynamic and uncertain project environments. Leadership development efforts should prioritize coaching and blended training approaches that build emotional intelligence, adaptability, and relational effectiveness. Future research should address underexplored contexts such as healthcare and smallto-medium enterprises, and employ longitudinal designs to assess the sustained impact of leadership behaviors on project outcomes.

title: Beyond Training: Worker Agency, Informal Learning, and Competition
affiliations: NHH Norwegian School of Economics and NHH Norwegian School of Economics - Department of Economics

detail.title: Beyond Training: Worker Agency, Informal Learning, and Competition

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper reconsiders how labor market competition shapes skill development --- integrating the perspectives of both firms and workers. We show that competition serves as a catalyst for learning. It creates outside opportunities which incentivize workers to invest in their own skills, and it imposes innovation pressure that raises the value of training for firms. Using linked Norwegian survey and administrative data together with vignette experiments, we find that workers in more competitive markets accumulate skills faster than workers in concentrated marketsprimarily through informal learningand that these gains are concentrated in higher-order, transferable skills. Firms in competitive environments also invest more in formal training, treating it as a strategic necessity rather than a dispensable cost. Experimental evidence complements these findings by showing that both workers and managers expect greater returns to learning and human capital investments in competitive markets. Together, these results challenge the canonical view of competition as a source of market failure in training and instead highlight its role in facilitating both worker-led and firm-led investments in human capital.

title: Stealing the Show? Foreign Cheerleaders and Baseball Fan Attendance in Taiwan's CPBL
affiliations: National Chung Cheng University - Department of Economics and National Chung Cheng University

detail.title: Stealing the Show? Foreign Cheerleaders and Baseball Fan Attendance in Taiwan's CPBL
detail.abstract: This paper examines the impact of foreign cheerleaders on stadium attendance in Taiwan's Chinese Professional Baseball League (CPBL). In March 2023, the Rakuten Monkeys signed South Korean cheerleader Lee Da-Hye, marking the first entry of a foreign cheerleader into the league. Her debut drew widespread attention, boosted attendance in 2023, and prompted other teams to recruit Korean cheerleaders in 2024. Using a panel dataset of 660 games from 2023 to 2024 and high-dimensional fixed-effects regressions, we estimate the effect of foreign cheerleaders on attendance. Results show that each additional foreign cheerleader increases attendance by about 5 percent on average. The effect was particularly strong in 2023, when Lee Da-Hye alone increased attendance by roughly 12 percent. However, the effect diminished in 2024 as foreign cheerleaders became more common, consistent with a novelty effect. Heterogeneity across teams further suggests that success may depend on differences in managerial capabilities. These findings contribute to the literature by identifying cheerleading as an overlooked demand shifter and by demonstrating the broader relevance of entertainment-driven strategies in professional sports.

title: A Brief Review of Political Identity
affiliations: Catholic University of Portugal, University of Texas at San Antonio and Boston College

detail.title: A Brief Review of Political Identity
detail.abstract:
“Identity” is a social category with which individuals associate themselves given certain attributes (Tajfel and Turner 1986). Many of those attributes are fixed such nationality, age and family background or hard to change such as gender, race or physique. Importantly though, people can assign their identity to the extent that identity is a “subjective or internalized sense of belonging to the group” (Huddy 2003, 513-14).

Political identity, the identification to a particular political group, is contingent on a lot of individual discretion. People can choose their political opinions and vote. However, recent research shows that political identity can override even relatively fixed demographically based identities such gender, class, religion and ethnicity (Egan 2020; Hopkins, Kaiser and Perez 2023; Huddy 2001; Margolis 2018). Some people adjust their demographic identities to better align with partisan and ideological prototypes including ethnicity (Hopkins et al. 2023), religion (Margolis 2018), and even sexual orientation (Egan 2020). Political identity has become key to the self-concept for some people, with implications far beyond shared policy preferences.

Identity signaling is an important motive for consumer behavior. Consumers purchase products not only to express their identity to themselves but also to communicate it outwardly (Belk, Bahn, and Mayer 1982; Bodner and Prelec 2003; Berger and Heath 2007; Dhar and Wertenbroch 2012). According to Forehand, Reed, and Saint Clair (2021), consumers may hold multiple identities interconnected with one another, each activated in a specific context or situation. These identities are linked in a network providing a collective sense of meaning to the person. Consumer learns the traits, attributes, or norms characterizing the group they identify with, and can, at times, form stereotypes associated with those groups (Srull and Wyer 1979). In essence, consumer identity is acquired over time, stored in memory, and reinforced by the environment, profoundly influencing consumers’ motivation and behavior.

This chapter analyzes the formation of political ideology in order to understand the expression of political identity through consumption. We first define political identity and political ideology. We then review the origins of political ideology. We then provide a brief review of consumer political identity to understand when and how political ideology is translated into consumer identity and consumer behavior. Finally, we generate testable hypotheses given social identity theory, the nature of political beliefs, and the factors that promote the categorization of oneself and others into groups.

title: Why Do Customers Keep Coming Back? The Moderating Role of Customer Perception of Influencer Marketing in Brand Attachment and Repurchase Behavior
affiliations: SEGi University, SEGi University Kota Damansara, SEGi University and Suzhou University

detail.title: Why Do Customers Keep Coming Back? The Moderating Role of Customer Perception of Influencer Marketing in Brand Attachment and Repurchase Behavior
detail.abstract:
The Chinese fast food industry has experienced sustained growth in recent years and
has secured a significant position in the global food service market. Brand attachment,
the deep emotional bond between consumers and brands, has been demonstrated to
accord material influence on brand loyalty and repurchase behavior. However, systematic
research remains limited and explores the accurate role of brand attachment in the
Chinese fast food sector. The study is based on attachment theory and has developed
a theoretical model to appraise how brand attachment affects repurchase behavior. The
model specifically evaluates the dual mediating roles of customer perceived value and
brand loyalty, as well as the moderating role of customer perceptions of influencer
marketing. Data were collected through questionnaires from 560 Chinese fast food
consumers in first-tier and new first-tier cities in China. The study employed PLS-SEM
for data analysis and produced the following results: (1) Brand attachment has significant
positive effects on repurchase behavior, customer perceived value, and brand loyalty;
(2) Brand attachment indirectly affects repurchase behavior through both customer
perceived value and brand loyalty, with the two playing a dual mediating role; (3)
Customer perceptions of influencer marketing significantly moderate the relationship
between brand attachment and repurchase behavior. These findings offer valuable
practical guidance for managing Chinese fast food brands and suggest that companies
should cultivate brand attachment to improve customer perceived value and brand
loyalty, finally driving repurchase behavior. Influencer marketing, as a potent brand
communication tool, should be fully utilized to amplify the effect of brand attachment
on consumer behavior. Further research could explore how brand attachment varies
across cultural backgrounds and its effect on consumer behavior.

AI.tldr: 本研究基于依恋理论，探讨品牌依恋通过顾客感知价值和品牌忠诚度的双重中介作用，以及网红营销感知的调节作用，如何影响中国快餐消费者的重复购买行为。研究发现品牌依恋对重复购买行为有显著正向影响，且网红营销感知能增强这种影响。

AI.theoretical_framework: 依恋理论
AI.method: 通过问卷调查收集中国一线和新一线城市560名快餐消费者的数据，采用PLS-SEM进行数据分析
AI.findings: 1) 品牌依恋对重复购买行为、顾客感知价值和品牌忠诚度有显著正向影响；2) 品牌依恋通过顾客感知价值和品牌忠诚度的双重中介作用间接影响重复购买行为；3) 顾客对网红营销的感知显著调节品牌依恋与重复购买行为之间的关系
AI.theory_contributions: 构建了基于依恋理论的理论模型，揭示了品牌依恋影响重复购买行为的内在机制（双重中介作用）和边界条件（网红营销感知的调节作用）
AI.practical_contributions: 为中国快餐品牌管理提供实践指导：企业应培养品牌依恋来提升顾客感知价值和品牌忠诚度，最终促进重复购买行为；应充分利用网红营销作为有效的品牌传播工具来放大品牌依恋对消费者行为的影响

affiliations: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, , Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, Brandeis University, Federal Reserve Bank of Boston and Federal Reserve Bank of Boston

detail.title: Effects of Tariff Uncertainty on the Outlook of Small and Medium-sized Businesses

publicationDetails.detailsText: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston Research Paper Series Current Policy Perspectives Paper No. 2025-12
publicationDetails.journalName: FRB-Boston: Research Department Current Policy Perspectives (Topic)

detail.abstract: A large body of research demonstrates that uncertainty affects many dimensions of firms’ decisions, from investment and hiring to pricing and profitability. To gain a better understanding of how uncertainty induced by shifting trade policy shapes the behavior of small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) the authors surveyed decision-makers at SMBs. The survey, administered by Morning Consult, was conducted in three waves: in December 2024, February 2025, and late April 2025. Each wave contained a nationally representative sample of about 600 SMBs.

AI.tldr: 本文通过三轮全国代表性调查（共约1800家中小企业），研究了贸易政策不确定性对中小企业决策行为的影响
AI.research_question: 贸易政策不确定性如何影响中小企业的行为决策？
AI.motivation: 现有研究表明不确定性影响企业多方面决策，但贸易政策不确定性对中小企业的影响机制尚不明确
AI.theoretical_framework: 不确定性理论、企业决策理论、贸易政策影响理论
AI.method: 三轮全国代表性问卷调查（2024年12月、2025年2月、2025年4月），每轮约600家中小企业，由Morning Consult执行

AI.practical_contributions: 为政策制定者和中小企业管理者提供应对贸易政策不确定性的实践指导

title: In Money, We Survive: The Effects of Social Security Retirement Income on Longevity
affiliations: Austin Peay State University and University of Wisconsin-Madison

detail.title: In Money, We Survive: The Effects of Social Security Retirement Income on Longevity

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: An old and debated line of research examines the income-mortality relationship and finds mixed evidence. In this paper, we re-evaluate previous studies using a new dataset and implementing a difference-in-difference model based on a Notch in Social Security retirement benefits to overcome selection and endogeneity issues. We employ Social Security Administration death records and find a positive income-longevity relationship. Moreover, we find more pronounced effects among low-educated individuals and people from low socioeconomic status families. Analyses using census data suggest that part of the reductions in retirement income are offset by wage income due to post-retirement labor force participation. Past age 80, the net adverse effects of the policy on both income and longevity become more pronounced.

AI.tldr: 本文通过使用社会保障退休福利的断点设计和差分法模型，重新评估了收入与死亡率的关系，发现收入与长寿之间存在正相关关系，特别是在低教育水平和社会经济地位较低的人群中更为明显。
AI.research_question: 收入与死亡率之间是否存在因果关系？收入如何影响个体的长寿？
AI.motivation: 以往关于收入与死亡率关系的研究存在混合证据，主要由于选择性和内生性问题。本文旨在通过新的数据和方法重新评估这一关系。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于健康经济学和劳动经济学理论，探讨收入对健康结果（特别是死亡率）的因果影响。
AI.method: 采用断点设计（Notch design）和差分法模型，利用社会保障管理局的死亡记录数据，克服选择性和内生性问题。
AI.findings: 发现收入与长寿之间存在正相关关系；效应在低教育水平和社会经济地位较低人群中更为明显；部分退休收入减少通过退休后劳动力参与获得工资收入来抵消；80岁后政策对收入和长寿的负面影响更加显著。
AI.theory_contributions: 为收入与健康关系的因果推断提供了新的实证证据；验证了断点设计在解决内生性问题上的有效性。
AI.practical_contributions: 为社会保障政策设计提供了重要参考；强调了关注弱势群体收入保障的重要性；对退休政策调整具有实践指导意义。
